This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the Claimants against the award dated 05.12.2020 passed by the learned 2nd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Katghora, Dist- Korba (CG) in M.A.C.T. Case No. 46/2017.
2.

2nd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Katghora, Dist- Korba (CG)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.13,21,180/- to the appellants/claimants on account of death of husband of appellant No.-1 Saraswati Koram, and son of the appellant Nos. 2 & 3 namely Gitaram & Savitri Bai respectively and father of appellant No.-4 Saraswati Koram vs Jagdish Prasad on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75335367/
1 Gareeman in a motor accident that took place on 27.02.2017 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle Trailer bearing registration No. CG-04-JB-1325, driven by respondent No-1 Jagdish Prasad, owned by respondent No-2 Ravi Shankar Dubey and insured by the respondent No-3 the New India Insurance Company Ltd.
3. As per the pleadings, the deceased Suresh Kumar Koram was working as a Driver and was earning Rs.8000/- per month.
The appellants/claimants were depending upon the income of the deceased.
4. The non applicants Respondent Nos- 1 and 2 were proceeded ex parte before the learned Claims Tribunal and have not contested the case.

5. The respondent No-3 the Insurance Company has filed its written statement and denied the averments of the claim application, and pleaded that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and therefore, there is a breach of Policy condition and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the learned Claims Tribunal has framed 6 issues and after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record, decided the same in favour of the appellants/claimants, and the Tribunal found the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.6,206/- per month and awarded the above stated compensation amount.

7. Mr. Palash Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellants submit that the deceased Suresh Kumar Koram was working as Driver and was earning Rs. 8000/-, he was aged about 24 years and therefore, his monthly income ought to have been considered as Rs.8000/- per month.

Alternatively, he submits that looking to the profession of the deceased and also the minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident, at least the minimum wages should have been taken into consideration for assessment of the compensation amount.

He would further submit that the amount awarded towards the other heads is also on the lower side and therefore the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is liable to be enhanced suitably.
8.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No-3 /Insurance Company supported the impugned award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal and submits that the claimants have not filed any document with regard to the income of the deceased and therefore learned Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased and had passed the award accordingly which is just and proper and the impugned award needs no interference by this court.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10. Barring the oral evidence of the appellants/claimants, the document Ex-P/9 was filed by the claimants/appellants in support of their claim that the deceased was working as Driver and was earning Rs. 8000/- per month.
The Driving license of the deceased Ex P/9 bears with the endorsement that he was granted license to drive the LMV.
However, there is no documentary evidence with respect to the monthly income of the deceased at the time of accident.

Looking to the nature of job of the deceased, the date of accident as also the minimum wages prevailing on the date Saraswati Koram vs Jagdish Prasad on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75335367/
2 of accident
, this Court is of the considered view that the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.7,500/- per month can be considered for computing the compensation.

11. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:
Monthly income of the deceased is Rs.7,500/- per month By adding 40% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, total monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,500 (7500 + 3000).
Total yearly income Rs 1,26,000/- (10,500 X 12) Out of this amount, 1/4th Personal expenditure to be deducted, now yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.94,500/-
Deceased was aged about 24 years at the time of accident, therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121, multiplier of 18 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.17,01,000/- (94,500 x 18).

For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.13,21,180/- already awarded by the Tribunal is now enhanced to Rs.18,91,000/-.

Hence, after deducting the amount Rs. 13,21,180/-, the claimants are held entitled for additional amount of Rs.5,69,820/- The additional amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.
On such deposit being made by the insurance company, Rs. 3,00,000/- shall be deposited in the name of Appellant No. 4 Gareeman up to his majority in FDR in any nationalized bank.

The remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants in the terms and proportion mentioned in Para 32 of the impugned award Saraswati Koram vs Jagdish Prasad on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75335367/
